title: God renews strength like eagles — Isaiah 40
paragraphs: God renews strength like eagles — Isaiah 40
He does not renew strength the way the world does.

Not by making you harder.
Not by making you louder.
Not by making you pretend you are okay.

Isaiah 40 says the Lord gives power to the faint, and to those who have no might, He increases strength. Then comes the promise: those who wait on the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles. They shall run and not be weary. They shall walk and not faint.
That means your exhaustion is not the end of your story.

God is not ashamed of your weakness. He meets you there. Eagles do not flap in panic to stay up—they rise on the wind. In the same way, the believer is not carried by self-effort, but by surrender. Waiting on the Lord is not doing nothing. It is trusting, praying, obeying, and leaning your full weight on the faithfulness of God.

And here’s what we miss: this promise is not just about surviving another day. It points us to Christ. Jesus carried the burden we could not carry, bore the sin we could not outrun, and rose with power we could never manufacture. So when your soul is collapsing, your strength is not found in yourself. It is found in Him.
Brother, sister—if you feel tired, empty, stretched thin—look up. The same God who made the eagle knows how to lift a weary heart.

Wait on Him.
Trust Him.
Stay with Him.
